initial_requirements: The Expanded Very Large Array needs an operations system for configuring and monitoring its radio-astronomy correlator and processing the resulting data stream in real time. Scientists and engineers should be able to inspect system health and observational data, while the software assembles and transforms correlator output into usable results for downstream storage and analysis. The system should identify faults and recover automatically where practical.

messages.content: What are the primary operational goals and core capabilities this system must deliver for configuring the correlator, monitoring system health, and processing the data stream in real time?

The main goal is to let operations staff set up the correlator for an observing run, verify that it is behaving correctly, and keep the data flowing without interruption. It also needs to take the raw correlator output, transform it into a usable form in real time, and hand it off for storage and later analysis.
On the monitoring side, people need a clear view of system health, current observing status, and the quality of the incoming data so they can spot issues quickly. Where possible, the system should detect faults on its own and recover automatically, since we can’t afford to lose data during an observation if we can avoid it.
